---
title: "SSH Failed Connection and Remedy"
author: "Moses Otieno"
date: "2025-01-07"
categories: [programming]
---

Connecting to a server remotely can sometimes be challenging, even if you have your SSH keys. For example, if you encounter the error `Permission denied (publickey)`, it means your machine is unable to communicate with the remote server.

This issue could occur if you've recently generated a new set of SSH keys, but those keys have not yet been added to the remote server.

To resolve this:

1.  Go to the machine having difficulty connecting to the server.

2.  Copy your public SSH key (usually found in `~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub`).

3.  Create a new ssh key then paste the key

And that's it! Problem solved.
